shortDescription: Thailand will extend its consumer subsidy programme using 40 billion baht ($1.20 billion) remaining from the first phase, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Friday.($1 = 33.2900 baht)

children: Thailand will extend its consumer subsidy programme using 40 billion baht ($1.20 billion) remaining from the first phase, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Friday.
The first phase covered about 43 million people and ran from June to September.
The government subsidised 60% of eligible purchases, capped at 200 baht per person per day.
The extension, subject to cabinet approval, is aimed at helping ease living costs.
"This is not a populist policy. It is both an economic stimulus policy and a measure to ease people's expenses across the country at a time of high living costs," Anutin said.
The extension will last two months, a government spokesperson said.
